newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: New S.Lanka court to try anti-terrorism detainees.
newsitem.headline: New S.Lanka court to try anti-terrorism detainees.

text.p: Sri Lanka will open a new high court next week to try people charged under the country's anti-terrorism law, a government minister said on Thursday.

Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister Gamini Peiris said the court, to be inaugurated on August 15 in the capital Colombo, was needed to quickly hear cases brought under the Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA).
"Although the main concern will be to dispose of cases under the PTA, it will have the jurisdiction of any other high court," Peiris told a news conference.
Figures from the Attorney-General's office show that 966 people have been indicted under the PTA since 1994.

Sri Lanka applies the Act to people suspected of being involved in terrorist activities, including helping Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels who are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the island's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the 14-year-old war. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
The government also operates emergency regulations to arrest those suspected of conspiring against the state.
The Attorney-General's office said 438 people were being tried under those laws.
The government plans to open another high court in northern Vavuniya town next month, which will try people charged under the country's laws, the minister said.
"We want to rekindle civil society that has been raged by the war for so long," Peiris said.
Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) northeast of the capital Colombo, has long been the frontier town in the country's ethnic war.
